map.Lessons 9-1 & 9-2 — part of the Cause &: Lessons 9-1 & 9-2 — part of the Cause & Effect arc. independent & dependent variables · reading graphs · 6.AT.D.11. Read straight through. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. No gate stops you.
map.Episode 1. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 1. Same crew, same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are ready.
map.The harvest dome feeds half of Axiom Cit: The harvest dome feeds half of Axiom City. It is wilting. Idris, you and me. We lead this one together.
map.Co-op mode accepted. Look — the mist is: Co-op mode accepted. Look, the mist is so thick the crops can't find the sun.
map.Wilting rows, runaway mist, temperature: Wilting rows. Too much mist. The temperature drifts all night. Everyone grab a sensor.
Distortion found: the climate system. Something in there has causes and effects mixed up.
map.Inside the dome. Fans the size of doors: Inside the dome. Fans as big as doors line the walls.
map.Test one. I run the fans; Owen reads the: Test one. I run the fans. Owen reads the thermometer. The longer the cooling fans run, the lower the dome temperature.
map.Confirmed. Fan time up, temperature down: Confirmed. Fan time goes up, temperature goes down. Every trial.
map.Name your players. The independent varia: Name your players. The independent variable is the one you change on purpose. It is the cause. The dependent variable answers it. It is the effect.
map.Two quantities, one relationship. Indepe: Two quantities, one relationship. Independent variable: the input you control. Dependent variable: the output that depends on it.
map.Game translation: independent is the but: In a game: independent is the button you press. Dependent is what happens on the screen.
map.Your turn, reader. Tag the variables bef: Your turn, reader. Tag the variables before we touch another dial.
map.Scenario from Sora's test: \"The longer: Sora's test says: "The longer the cooling fans run, the lower the dome temperature." Tag both variables. Pick one answer in EACH group.
map.Conceptual: the independent variable is: Conceptual: the independent variable is the cause. You set it on purpose. The dependent variable is the effect. It reacts. You can't set it directly.
map.Procedural: try the plant test first: yo: Procedural: try the plant test first. You choose how much water to give (you set it, so independent). The plant's growth answers (dependent). Now read the fan sentence the same way. Which quantity gets SET? Which one REACTS?
map.VEX logged last night's temperature. A g: VEX logged last night's temperature. A graph is a picture of the relationship. Time goes across the bottom. Temperature goes up the side.
map.Reading order: left to right. Like a sen: Reading order: left to right. Like a sentence.
map.This line falls steadily, then levels of: This line falls steadily, then goes flat. Falling means cooling. Flat means holding.
map.A graph shows how the dependent variable: A graph shows how the dependent variable (up the side) changes as the independent variable (across the bottom) increases.
map.Match the graph to its story, reader. Th: Match the graph to its story, reader. The dome is talking. Listen with your eyes.
map.VEX projects last night's log: the line: VEX shows last night's log: the line falls steadily, then levels off flat. Which story does this graph tell? Tap the matching card, then CHECK.
map.Conceptual: a graph reads like a sentenc: Conceptual: a graph reads like a sentence, left to right. Time passes as you move right. The line's height is the temperature at that time.
map.Procedural: split the line into its two: Procedural: split the line into its two pieces, in order. Piece one slants down. What is the temperature doing? Piece two is level. What is it doing now? Find the story with those two parts in that order.
map.The full story — Cause & Effect — is glo: The full story, Cause & Effect, is glowing at the city gate. — A.V.
map.Next up: the full anchor volume — Cause: Next up: the full anchor volume, Cause & Effect.
map.Different scenario: 'The more minutes a: A new scenario: 'The more minutes a candle burns, the shorter it gets.'
map.Burn time is the quantity being allowed: Burn time is the quantity that changes on purpose. It is the independent variable (the cause).
map.The candle's height responds to that tim: The candle's height reacts to that time. It is the dependent variable (the effect).
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new example:
map.In 'the more laps you swim, the more tir: In 'the more laps you swim, the more tired you feel', which is the dependent variable: laps or tired?
map.A different graph: a line that climbs st: A new graph: a line that climbs steadily, then goes flat.
map.Climbing piece = the quantity is increas: Climbing piece = the quantity is going up, like a bathtub filling.
map.Flat piece = no change — the tap is off;: Flat piece = no change. The tap is off. The level stays. Story: 'it rises, then stays put.'
map.On a graph, a line that stays flat the w: On a graph, a line that stays flat the whole time shows a quantity that is… (write: changing or constant)
map.Pick one tag in EACH group — a cause and: Pick one tag in EACH group. Pick a cause and an effect.
map.Fan time is the cause you control; the t: Fan time is the cause you control. The temperature answers it. Tagged and logged!
map.Swapped! That's the old controller's exa: Swapped! That is the old controller's mistake. The temperature does not make the fans run.
map.The fans' color never changes and change: The fans' color never changes. It changes nothing. It is not a variable in this story.
map.The crops care about the result, but the: The crops care about the result. But they are not one of the two changing quantities in the sentence.
map.One tag is off. Ask: which quantity do w: One tag is off. Ask: which quantity do we SET? Which one REACTS?
map.Falling line, then flat line — cooling,: Falling line, then flat line: cooling, then holding. You read the dome's story well.
map.Read left to right, like a sentence — on: Read left to right, like a sentence. On this graph the FALL comes first, then the flat part.
map.Rising first would slant UP at the start: Rising first would slant UP at the start. But this line starts by falling. It never climbs back.
map.Falling then rising would make a V shape: Falling then rising would make a V shape. After the fall, this line stays flat.
